header.title: Εἰδύλλια: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Theocritus
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tlg0005.tlg001.perseus-grc2, from the Perseus Digital Library (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.

notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0005.tlg001.perseus-: In 2.15 the participle 'making' (ἔρδοισα) may refer to Hecate or to the speaker.
θάψος (2.88) is a plant yielding a yellow dye; its exact identity is uncertain.
Line 2.60 ends obscurely (ἇς ἔτι καὶ νύξ, literally 'of which still also night'); 'while it is still night' is a guess. Line 2.61 is absent from this text, so the sentence is incomplete as it stands.
The plant names (ἀσπάλαθος, παλίουρος, ἄχερδος) are given common equivalents; their exact identifications are uncertain.
τηλέφιλον ('love-in-absence', 3.29) is a leaf slapped on the arm as a love test; the plant is uncertain. Παραιβάτις (3.32) is printed as a name, but may be a description ('one who walks alongside').

nodes.text: I will go to Timagetus's wrestling school
tomorrow, to see him, and I will reproach him for the way he treats me.
But now I will bind him with burnt offerings. Come, Moon,
shine fair; for to you I will chant softly, goddess,
and to Hecate below the earth, before whom even the dogs tremble
as she goes among the tombs of the dead and the dark blood.
Hail, grim Hecate, and attend us to the end,
making these drugs no weaker than Circe's
or Medea's or golden-haired Perimede's.
*Iynx* [magic wheel], draw that man of mine to my house.
First the barley meal is burning in the fire. Come, sprinkle it on,
Thestylis. Wretch, where have your wits flown off to?
on Dia forgot fair-tressed Ariadne.
*Iynx* [magic wheel], draw that man of mine to my house.
*Hippomanes* [horse-madness] is a plant in Arcadia; for it all
the fillies and swift mares run mad over the mountains.
So may I see Delphis too, and may he cross into this house
like a madman, out from the glistening wrestling school.
*Iynx*, draw that man of mine to my house.
This fringe from his cloak Delphis lost,
and now I shred it and throw it into the fierce fire.
Ah, tormenting Love, why the dark blood from my flesh
have you clung like a marsh leech and drunk it all?
*Iynx*, draw that man of mine to my house.
I will grind a lizard and take him an evil drink tomorrow.
Thestylis, now take these herbs and smear them
on the upper part of his doorpost, while it is still night,
and say as you spit: 'I knead the bones of Delphis.'
*Iynx*, draw that man of mine to my house.
Now that I am alone, where shall I begin to weep for my love?
and I lay on my bed ten days and ten nights.
Consider my love, where it came from, lady Moon.
And often my skin turned the colour of yellow dye-wood,
and all the hair fell from my head, and what was left
was only bones and skin. And to whose house did I not go,
or what old woman's house did I pass by, any who knew charms?
But there was no relief; and the time slipped by in flight.
Consider my love, where it came from, lady Moon.
But now it is the twelfth day since I have so much as seen him.
Has he not found some other delight, and forgotten me?
For now I will bind him with these love charms; but if he still
hurts me, by the Fates, he will knock at the gate of Hades.
Such evil drugs, I tell you, I keep for him in a box,
my lady, which I learned of from an Assyrian stranger.
But you, fare well, and turn your horses towards Ocean,
lady; and I will bear my longing as I have endured it.
where Olpis the fisherman watches for tunny;
and if I die, that at least will have been sweet to you.
I learned it lately, when I was wondering whether you love me:
not even the love-in-absence leaf, the smacker, stuck fast,
but simply withered away on my soft forearm.
And a country sieve-diviner told the truth too,
Paraebatis, who was gathering herbs the other day: that I
am wholly given over to you, but you take no account of me.
And yet I am keeping for you a white goat, mother of twins,
which Mermnon's dark-skinned hired girl, too,
as I judge it, it looked so; and of my teeth
it showed a gleam whiter than Parian stone.
But so as not to be struck by the evil eye, I spat three times into my breast;
for the old woman Cotyttaris taught me that,
who just lately piped for the reapers at Hippocion's.
Having said so much, Damoetas kissed Daphnis,
and get ready dry sticks of camel-thorn or of Christ's thorn
or bramble, or a withered wild pear shaken by the wind;
and burn these two serpents on the wild faggots
at midnight, the hour when they wanted to kill your child.
At dawn let one of your maids gather the ash of the fire
and carry it, every bit, and throw it well across the river
onto the jagged rocks, beyond the borders, and come back
without turning round. And fumigate the house with pure sulphur
first, and then, mixed with salt, as is the custom,
sprinkle untainted water with a garlanded branch;
and sacrifice a male pig to Zeus the Uppermost,
so that you may always prove uppermost over your enemies.
He spoke, and pushing back his ivory chair, he went,
